WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT. It is not a list of things currently broken, and it is not a place
to park a red test. Every entry names a root cause with a file:line and the workstream that
owns the fix. Adding an entry to make CI green is the one use of this file that is
forbidden; if a new failure appears, it is a regression until someone proves otherwise.

ALSO CORRECTED: this block used to say the required `tests` job 'cannot pass until the dead

There is deliberately NO section for errors. The suite's zero-errors property is enforced
unconditionally: an error means a test could not run at all.
2026-10-17 -- SIX ENTRIES DELETED BECAUSE THEY NOW PASS, WHICH THIS GATE REQUIRES.
NEW-ADDON-SCHEMA-02 is FIXED, so the six guest-screen entries that named it have been
removed from expected_failures. Deleting them is not rebaselining and not suppression --
it is the opposite, and it is mandatory: this gate asserts the set in BOTH directions, so

resources/views/layouts/guest.blade.php:96 renders. The fix is in app/ and NOT in
packages/workdo/, so guard-no-workdo-changes.sh is satisfied and no vendored commercial
file was edited -- which is what the deleted entries recorded as the blocker.

_require_reason_log_note: Fail the gate if no --log-teamcity log is supplied. The skip REASONS cannot be read from
JUnit at all -- PHPUnit 11.5.57 writes a bare <skipped/> with no message -- so the reason
half of the gate depends on a second log. Making its absence a FAILURE is what stops one
dropped CI flag from disabling a control in silence.
_minimum_testcases_note: A floor, not the count. Its only job is to stop the gate passing on a log from a run that
died early -- every set comparison in the checker is trivially satisfied by an empty log.
The real count at the time of writing is 1126 Feature testcases. Lower this ONLY when tests
are removed on purpose, and record why here.

Tests\\Feature\\Auth\\RegistrationTest::.cause: A FIXTURE GAP THAT EXPOSES A LATENT ROBUSTNESS DEFECT -- not the casing bug, and not what an earlier version of this entry claimed. CORRECTED AFTER MEASUREMENT: there is no addRole call at RegisteredUserController.php:249 (that line is a comment), the two real call sites are :179 and :310, and BOTH are null-guarded by `if ($role_r)`. Nothing dies: POST /register returns 302 and the request completes. Measured on a fresh test database, `roles` holds 0 rows and Role::where('name','admin')->first() is NULL, because RefreshDatabase runs migrations and not seeders. So the guard works exactly as written and the role assignment is SILENTLY SKIPPED: the user, the store and the login are committed and the merchant ends up with no role and no error. The test asserts the role, which is the property that matters. In production the admin role IS seeded, so this is latent rather than live -- but the silent tolerance is the real finding: a missing admin role provisions a merchant with no role and reports success.
Tests\\Feature\\Auth\\RegistrationTest::.owner: app/ -- NOT owned by the CI workstream. Needs a null guard plus a decision about what to do when the role is absent (the half-provisioned row should not survive).
Tests\\Feature\\Auth\\RegistrationTest::.proof_it_is_not_the_casing_bug: tests/Feature/Platform/AddonMigrationStrandingTest.php shows POST /register still fails to assign the role with every stranded table present.

Tests\\Feature\\ProfileTest::test_profil.cause: A REAL APPLICATION DEFECT, and a DIFFERENT one from the other seven. GET /profile answers 500 with ErrorException: Attempt to read property "slug" on null at app/Http/Controllers/HomeController.php:367 (`route('landing_page', $store->slug)`). /profile is served by UserController@profile, not by Breeze's ProfileController@edit, so this test exercises the real merchant profile page.
Tests\\Feature\\ProfileTest::test_profil.owner: app/ -- NOT owned by the CI workstream. Needs a null-store guard at HomeController.php:367 (and :369, the same expression in the sibling branch).
Tests\\Feature\\ProfileTest::test_profil.proof_it_is_not_the_casing_bug: tests/Feature/Platform/AddonMigrationStrandingTest::test_the_profile_page_failure_is_not_this_bug asserts the 500 persists with every stranded table present, and reddens if it is ever fixed.
